(1) RFC 9484 CONNECT-IP over HTTP/3 for the Cloudflare WARP configuration: the base64 SEC1 P-256 client key generates the pinned adapter's self-signed client certificate, `public-key` (a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo) pins the endpoint certificate, and the request is `:method CONNECT`, `:protocol cf-connect-ip`, `:scheme https`, `:authority`/`:path` from `uri` (default https://cloudflareaccess.com) with `capsule-protocol: ?1`. ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT is sent and ADDRESS_ASSIGN/ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT are read; whole IPv4/IPv6 packets travel as HTTP Datagrams. UDP is served by the in-tree UDP codec and TCP by the in-tree minimal TCP client (`outbound/tcp.rs`: active open, SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK, data/ACK, FIN/RST, MSS and peer-window limits, retransmission with RFC 6298-style backoff, fast retransmit, in-order delivery with bounded reordering, half-close); one tunnel and one TCP connection per `dial`. the `ip`, `ipv6`, `mtu`, `ip-stack`, `remote-dns-resolve` and `dns` options keep their T18 semantics. (2) The RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset from T14 still serves a plain server with `udp: true`; it carries UDP only (RFC 9298 has no TCP path), so a TCP dial through that shape is refused by name. `network: h2|h3-l4proxy`, the QUIC congestion-controller options, `dialer-proxy`, gVisor and passive/simultaneous-open TCP are named.

CONNECT-UDP: one request stream per destination, DATAGRAM capsules with context ID 0, closed flows reclaimed before the cap is enforced.

Every proxy type outside the implemented ones is rejected at load time with its type named, never ignored; familiesNotImplemented records the task that implements it.
Rule types UID/DSCP/IN-USER/IN-NAME/REMATCH-NAME/PROCESS-*-WILDCARD are rejected by name. PASS/PASS-RULE markers and proxy-group targets are T23.
GEOIP/IP-ASN/IP-CIDR rules match a destination only when it is already an IP; DNS/hosts (T22) provide name resolution. A warning records this at load.
geodata-mode false uses Country.mmdb; geodata-mode true uses GeoIP.dat; GEOSITE always uses GeoSite.dat. MRS rule-provider decoding shares the Tauri mrs.rs algorithm (ported, not shared code).
Proxy-provider health-check fields are parsed and exposed but latency probing is T23; provider updates are exposed through Kernel::update_*_provider for T25.

notImplementedOnPlatform.windows: sessions compile but the platform session/TUN path is T6; no Windows run has been recorded

platform.note: Every runtime result here comes from macOS arm64, including the UDP and private-CA cases. A platform difference must be reproduced against the same-platform Mihomo; nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run.

rust.note: rustMapping on each entry comes from that file; partial entries name the options they reject, unimplemented entries are rejected at load time and are never compatible.

coverage.note: mapped counts only entries the Rust kernel implements and tests observe; partial and unimplemented entries are not compatibility claims.
